# Presence, Not Activity

Online systems usually treat activity as evidence that people are present.
Clicks, comments, views, and transactions become proxies for participation.

That assumption weakens when synthetic systems can produce the same signals
at enormous scale. More activity no longer necessarily means more people.

ÆPOCH reframes the problem around proofs of human presence. The aim is not to
ban automation, but to let human participation remain legible beside it.

The next internet must recognize presence, not just activity.
